category_title: At-risk four-year-olds from low-income families with context-dependent oral language proficiency
student_description: This student is an at-risk four-year-old with delayed language development who frequently defaults to one-word responses with adults due to a fear of making grammatical errors. While they can use more complex language with peers, they uniquely require adults to actively model complete sentences, recast their short answers with elaboration, and ask open-ended questions rather than relying on compliance-based directions or low-level recall questions.

criteria.rationale: Asking open-ended questions prevents the student from defaulting to their habit of giving one-word responses and encourages them to attempt more complex language.
criteria.check: The tutor asks at least one open-ended question that requires more than a single word to answer, avoiding simple yes/no or basic recall questions.

criteria.rationale: Restating and expanding on the student's brief answers provides a safe, non-judgmental model of correct grammar and complex sentence structure, addressing their fear of making errors.
criteria.check: The tutor responds to the student's utterance by restating it as a complete sentence, adding descriptive detail, or gently correcting grammar without explicitly stating the student was wrong.

criteria.rationale: Focusing on behavioral directions shuts down the student's willingness to speak, whereas prioritizing conversational engagement encourages verbal risk-taking.
criteria.check: The tutor engages the student in a back-and-forth verbal exchange rather than issuing a behavioral command or a 'listen and obey' directive.
